series_note: Salaries of office became percentages of the base salary on 7 December 1999 (Tribunal Report 99/01, Determination 1999/16). Before that they were fixed dollar amounts, which this series does not carry.

licences.federal_register_of_legislation: CC BY 4.0: based on content from the Federal Register of Legislation at 17 September 2026. For the latest information on Australian Government legislation please go to https://www.legislation.gov.au.
licences.parliamentary_handbook: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (Parliament of Australia website). Facts of office and dates only; served on Opax pages, never loaded into the knowledge box.

method: For each day a person sat in the federal parliament: the parliamentary base salary then in force, plus the additional salary of the post they then held, as a percentage of that base. A Minister is paid the one ministerial rate that applies. Other office holders are paid the sum of the percentages of their offices, rounded up to the next $10; a shadow minister is paid a flat rate instead. Yearly figures add those days across a financial year. Nothing is adjusted for inflation.

not_covered.text: Committee chairs and deputy chairs are paid a further 3% to 16% that is not counted, because the Parliamentary Handbook gives no dates for who chaired what.
A shadow minister is paid a loading only if named in the Opposition Leader’s notice to the Clerks, which is capped and not published; Opax assumes every listed shadow minister is named.

electorate_allowance.source: Remuneration Tribunal (Members of Parliament) Determination 2026, section 8: $39,700 for a senator or an electorate under 2,000 km2, $47,200 under 5,000 km2, $57,100 above.
